In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photoelectron spectra are consistent with a reaction mechanism in which the anion dissociates to form OH−+NH3 and the neutral is produced from the reactant channel.
OH−(NH2) is the most stable species in the OH−(NHn) system and that the OH−(OH) species has a very high barrier to reaction.
the photoelectron spectrum of the OH−(NH2) complex exhibits a broad band with a peak maximum at approximately 2.5 eV, and that this band is due to the OH(NH2) neutral.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OH−(NH)2 anion is bound by 0.6 eV, and the OH−(2NH3) anion by 1.0 eV.
the OH−(NH) anion is a bound species with an electron affinity of 2.35 eV.
the anions OH−(NH4) and OH−(NH2)−NH3 are the primary products from the 351 nm photodetachment of OH−(H2O)n n=1–2 and OH−(HOD)n n=1.
